briefing.opening: Good morning/afternoon. We will now begin the climate briefing for September 10, 2026.

sections.title: 🔴 Deepening Global Climate Crisis and Extreme Phenomena
sections.content: Reports from services like Copernicus Climate Change Service continue to indicate that August 2026 globally recorded a joint highest temperature on record, with global temperatures once again rising more than 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels [197, 200, 207, 219, 222, 225, 227]. Research suggesting that the strengthening Super El Niño phenomenon and climate change are exacerbating it [217] is leading to a frequent occurrence of extreme weather events [201], with an increase in emergency room visits due to heat-related illnesses in the United States [203]. Recently, large-scale floods in Nepal have resulted in numerous casualties and missing persons [195, 196, 214, 23, 4, 25], which is analyzed as a complex impact of warming in the Himalayan region and climate change [214]. Furthermore, the impacts on the overall economy are also intensifying, including increased maritime transportation costs due to the declining water level of the Caspian Sea [1, 7] and disruption in the fashion industry along with the 'fashionflation' phenomenon caused by unpredictable seasonal changes [5, 9, 12]. Analyses indicating that the climate crisis is affecting corporate finance and transforming ESG from a mere disclosure into a survival strategy [15], along with research suggesting that climate feedback loops could worsen global warming by 30% [209, 228], once again underscore the severity of the crisis we face.

sections.title: 🇰🇷 Accelerating Domestic Efforts for Carbon Neutrality
sections.content: Domestically, various efforts to achieve carbon neutrality are bearing fruit. Several local governments, including Gunpo City [3, 14], Paju City [27, 29, 64, 65, 68, 94, 95], and Pyeongtaek City [38, 97], have received prestigious awards such as the 'Korea Urban Awards,' recognizing the excellence of their climate change response and carbon neutrality policies. Notably, Changwon City achieved the remarkable feat of ranking first for two consecutive years in the carbon neutrality assessment for basic local governments [36, 69, 89, 92], and both Chungcheongnam-do Province [35, 63, 75, 101, 105, 107] and Gyeongsangnam-do Province [66, 81, 104] were highly praised as excellent examples of carbon neutrality. In the corporate sector, KEPCO KPS is operating 'ESG Youth-lab' to identify carbon neutrality tasks with university students and local communities [40, 50, 55, 56, 98], and Korea Western Power is demonstrating active participation by issuing 50 billion won worth of green bonds to secure investment funds for carbon neutrality [54, 71, 78, 79]. Furthermore, Gwangmyeong City is investing 16 billion won to build a 'Carbon Neutral Smart City' model and showcase it at the 'World Smart City Expo' [31, 32, 33, 52, 53, 59, 74, 77, 87, 90, 91, 93, 108], accelerating the transition to a carbon-neutral society through cooperation between local governments and businesses.

sections.title: 🌱 Efforts to Strengthen Climate Change Adaptation and Resilience
sections.content: Adaptation efforts to prepare for the inevitable impacts of climate change are also actively underway. While investments in climate crisis 'adaptation' are being made globally [11], concrete action plans are also being developed domestically. Seoul City is actively commencing the creation of station-area residential complexes designed to cope with climate change, including heatwaves [8], and the Ministry of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs plans to further expand reservoir dredging by 8.38 million cubic meters by 2030 to strengthen disaster response capabilities against droughts and floods [13, 19]. The Jeonnam Regional Headquarters of Korea Rural Community Corporation is establishing a smart disaster management system [18], and Bucheon City is holding an interim reporting session for the establishment of its 3rd Climate Crisis Adaptation Plan [20], showcasing proactive responses from various local governments. Internationally, efforts to build climate-resilient cities are crucial, as exemplified by Chicago being selected as the world's number one city for climate change resilience [198]. Cases of strengthening climate change response capabilities through international cooperation, such as the Korea Rural Community Corporation transferring agricultural water management know-how to Bolivia [24], are also noteworthy.

sections.title: ⚠️ Expansion of Renewable Energy Transition and Current Challenges
sections.content: The transition to renewable energy is accelerating both domestically and internationally. LS Electric and Korea Midland Power have signed a large-scale cooperation agreement for the joint development and expansion of full-cycle renewable energy projects, including wind, solar, and BESS (Battery Energy Storage Systems), thereby changing the landscape of domestic renewable energy [112, 113, 115, 116, 118, 120, 124, 125, 126, 127, 129, 133, 137, 139, 141, 142, 143, 145, 146, 149, 150, 151, 153, 154, 155, 156, 157, 160, 161, 164, 165, 166, 167, 168, 169, 174, 175, 177, 178, 179, 180, 181, 182, 183, 185, 186, 188, 192]. Furthermore, social support is high, with over 63% of the public supporting the mandatory use of renewable energy for mega-project power [110, 114, 119, 122, 128, 132, 148, 191]. The government is also striving to strengthen industrial competitiveness by launching the 'Solar Industry Competitiveness Committee' to rebuild the solar supply chain and preempt next-generation technologies, setting a target of 87GW by 2030 [135, 170, 173]. However, challenges for stable power grid operation remain, such as concerns raised about the 'exaggeration' of renewable energy generation [109] and the government's response to power surplus caused by decreased electricity demand in autumn and increased renewable energy generation [111, 162]. We must successfully lead this major energy transition towards renewable energy by addressing these challenges.

briefing.closing: Today's briefing highlights the diverse efforts being made both domestically and internationally towards carbon neutrality, renewable energy transition, and climate adaptation, even amidst the threats of climate change. We must continue to foster a more sustainable future through ongoing cooperation and technological innovation. This concludes today's climate briefing.
